facts.text: Sonoma State University opened in 1960 as Sonoma State College, a teacher‑education center for the North Bay.
The campus’s Jean and Charles Schulz Information Center, finished in 2000, now holds over 400,000 books and a 750,000‑volume automated retrieval system.
Students can earn wine‑industry degrees at Sonoma State’s Wine Business Institute, a program that began in 1996 amid the region’s famed vineyards.
Six on‑campus villages—Cabernet, Zinfandel, Verdot, Sauvignon, Beaujolais, and Tuscany—play off the university’s wine‑country setting.
In spring 2020, Sonoma State cut men’s tennis, women’s tennis, and women’s water polo due to funding shortages.
The university’s library, a 215,000‑square‑foot building, features a computer‑managed shelving system that stores an additional 750,000 volumes beyond its physical stacks.
